A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Loopholing Discrete Diffusion work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, text-generation, arithmetic-reasoning, and ablation results in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments on idle steps, model scale, continued pre-training, propagation controls, and reasoning evaluation protocols.

M1.justification: The proposed latent pathway, LayerNorm fusion, two-pass self-conditioning objective, and generation/training algorithms remain unchanged. Section 3 makes sequence notation and conditioning arguments explicit; the new experiments apply the existing method or test a control variant.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LM1B/OWT training coverage, zero-shot corpora, downstream language tasks, and Countdown/Game of 24 tasks. The added experiments vary model capacity, training history, or evaluation procedures within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix D.11/Table 19 adds LDDM-M (sampled token) as a control against MDLM and LDDM-M (latent). This is a newly evaluated comparator; the original comparison methods remain present.

E3.justification: New protocols include 100K-step comparisons at 169M/424M parameters, continued pre-training from a 1M-step MDLM checkpoint for 10K–200K steps, and a matched 200K-step propagation-control experiment. Appendix D.12 adds the original MGDM evaluation-and-decoding scheme; v1's Table 4 already tested original decoding with stricter validity checks. Main experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices D.8–D.12 substantially extend the analyses: directly quantifying idle steps, testing capacity scaling and checkpoint adaptation, separating sampled-token from latent propagation, and checking reasoning results under alternative evaluation rules. These supplement v1's existing self-conditioning, propagation-length, MLP, multistep-backpropagation, and compute-budget studies.

E5.justification: The four GPT-4.1 evaluations per sequence, averaging practices, and Figure 4(b) error bars are unchanged. v2 adds no documented training-seed repetitions, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: Original benchmark tables and performance plots retain their results after matching renumbering. Substantial new results include 55.04 versus 93.71 Gen PPL for latent versus sampled-token propagation under the matched 200K-step setting (Table 19), and 51.51 after 200K continued pre-training steps (Table 18). Idle-step counts, scaling results, and original-protocol reasoning scores are also added. The introduction corrects the MDLM/AR Gen PPL ratio from 3.26 to 3.17.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and derivations remain substantively unchanged. Explicit conditioning arguments, positional indices, and renaming the self-conditioning loss to the Loopholing loss clarify notation without changing mathematical content; no new proofs or theorems appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the sampling-wall diagnosis, deterministic latent-path contribution, efficient self-conditioning, and language-generation/reasoning improvement claims. The added no-unrolling phrase restates a capability already explained in v1.

C2.justification: v1 reports unsuccessful initial attempts to add Loopholing through fine-tuning; v2 removes that limitation and interprets Tables 17–18 as demonstrating successful integration into pretrained checkpoints. New discussion also attributes gains specifically to pre-sampling latent propagation and argues that benefits persist at increased capacity. Section 6.3 narrows the early-TKL interpretation from faster denoising progress to more active prediction updates.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Reproducibility Statement providing a repository link for source code and processing/training/evaluation scripts. It also documents the 424M configuration and checkpoint initialization for continued pre-training. The extensive original hardware, optimizer, preprocessing, and pseudocode disclosures remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and main related-work section are retained. Appendix D.11 adds a limited positioning refinement by explicitly contrasting latent propagation with a sampled-token variant described as closer to standard self-conditioning, citing the already included Chen et al. work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and notation explanations clearer, revises the training introduction, adds cross-references and a reproducibility statement, and updates correspondence, acknowledgments, and publication headers. New appendix subsections extend the document without extensively rewriting or reorganizing its existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds six experimental tables (15–20) and the idle-step plot (Figure 8), substantially expanding the appendix displays. Existing sample figures gain colored error annotations and explanatory captions. Original performance plots are unchanged; other edits include loss-label and G-eval-caption corrections, table renumbering, and pseudocode reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis and practical applicability of the paper. The matched sampled-token control tests the central information-preservation mechanism more directly, while successful continued pre-training addresses v1's reported failure to adapt existing checkpoints. Evaluation under the original MGDM rules adds useful robustness evidence. One qualification remains: Table 16 repeats earlier 1M-step small-model scores within a section describing 100K-step training, leaving its cross-scale budget comparability unclear. This limits that scaling evidence but does not outweigh the other substantive gains.
